title: Ask for help the right way

explanation.text: Every programmer gets stuck. What matters is how you ask. A clear question gets a fast, useful answer. A vague one gets questions back or no answer at all. This works the same with a teacher, a friend, a forum, or an AI assistant.

items: **Actual**: what happened instead. Paste the **whole** error message.
**Code**: the smallest code that shows the problem, and that runs by itself.
**Setup**: your Python version and your system (for example Windows 11).

explanation.text: **Make the problem small.** Delete everything that is not needed to show the bug. Many times you find the answer while you do this.
**Be kind and short.** Say what you need in the first lines. Say thank you. Use simple words: the reader may not speak English as a first language, either.
Never paste secrets: API keys, passwords, or real private data. Replace them with fake values like "YOUR-KEY-HERE" before you share any code.

explanation.title: Question for help
explanation.text: Fill in each part with your own details. Delete a line if it does not apply.
explanation.code:
Title: [short and specific: what fails, and where]

Goal: I want to [what you want to do].

Expected: I thought [what should happen].

Actual: Instead, [what happens]. This is the full error:
[paste the whole error message]

I tried: [what you already tried, even if it failed]

My code (small and complete):
[paste the smallest code that shows the problem]

Setup: Python [version], [Windows 11 / other]

Thank you!

examples.title: A weak title and a better title
examples.code:
Weak: "Help, my code doesn't work!!"
Better: "KeyError: 'age' when I read a row from my CSV with csv.DictReader"

examples.title: A weak question and a better one
examples.code:
Weak: "My program crashes. What is wrong?"
Better: "I want to add up the 'amount' column of customers.csv. I expected a number, but I get ValueError: could not convert string to float: '$120.50'. I tried float(row['amount']). Here is a 6-line example that shows it. Python 3.12, Windows 11."

quiz.question: Which part of a question is the most important to paste in full?
quiz.explanation: The full error message tells the helper exactly what Python said.

quiz.question: Why make your example code small?
options: It is more polite to write less
The bug is easier to see, and you may find it yourself
quiz.explanation: A small example removes the noise. Often the answer shows up while you shrink it.

quiz.question: Before sharing code to get help, what should you remove?
quiz.explanation: Secrets and private data must never be shared. Use fake values.
